title: Why patients return to hospital from hospital at home: a qualitative study with patients, carers and clinicians
abstract: Aim: to explain how readmissions within 30 days of hospital-at-home care come about. Design: qualitative interviews with patients, family carers and clinicians anchored to recent readmissions, analysed with reflexive thematic analysis. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Hospital at home achieves readmission rates similar to ward care in trials, but local services see returns they cannot explain. Few studies report the views of patients and carers about how a readmission came about.
methods: About 36 participants in three groups (patients, carers, clinicians) were sampled purposively around recent readmissions and interviewed within four weeks, with record summaries to anchor their accounts. Two analysts with different backgrounds used reflexive thematic analysis.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present themes by participant group and the accounts of shared episodes.
discussion: The discussion will relate the themes to night-time escalation, carer strain and handover, and compare accounts of the same episodes across groups. It will state which changes the program could test before adding beds.
limitations: The study covers one program, and accounts given after a readmission are subject to recall. Clinicians may be reluctant to describe their own decisions.
conclusion: To be written after analysis. It will offer explanations and candidate changes, not rates.
